title: Microsoft 365 admin center: Organizational messages now supports hybrid-joined devices
summary: The briefing passes: hybrid-joined support, Windows requirements, licensing and the documented control operations are supported. The Intune API is valid despite the automatic warning; minor path omissions and an unsupported attribution of admin time to Learn should be corrected.

claims.claim: The roadmap record was modified at 2026-08-24T22:41:12.
Admins author and schedule in-product organizational messages in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: You can centrally manage organizational messages in the Microsoft 365 admin center. ... Control timing and frequency — Schedule start and end dates, set how often a message reappears, or send a one-time urgent message immediately.

claims.claim: Windows delivery supports only Microsoft Entra ID-joined and Microsoft Entra hybrid joined devices.
claims.quote: Devices - (For Windows) Only Microsoft Entra ID–joined devices and Microsoft Entra hybrid joined devices are supported.

claims.claim: The Learn page gives general Windows configuration without separate hybrid-specific configuration or prerequisites.
claims.quote: Searched: organizational messages hybrid joined enable default unmanaged configuration prerequisites; read the organizational messages main page and FAQ, including Requirements and Set tenant policies. No separate hybrid-specific configuration is given.

claims.claim: Windows channel recipients require Windows 11, version 25H2 or 24H2 Enterprise.
claims.quote: any message configured to be delivered to a Windows channel, like Windows Spotlight or Taskbar requires that recipients use Windows 11, version 25H2 and 24H2 Enterprise.

claims.claim: The Windows taskbar experience requires KB5094126.
claims.quote: Access to the Taskbar experience requires KB5094126 for Windows 11, version 25H2 and 24H2.

claims.claim: Government environments such as GCC and GCC-H are not supported at this time.
claims.quote: No, government environments such as GCC or GCC-H aren't supported at this time.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the arrival default of the hybrid-joined support change.
claims.quote: Searched: organizational messages hybrid joined separate enable disable switch default rollout; read roadmap description, organizational messages main page and FAQ. They document eligible devices and message authoring, not the arrival default of this support extension.

claims.claim: The sources do not state how the support extension changes existing messages or existing delivery behaviour.
claims.quote: Searched: organizational messages hybrid joined separate enable disable switch default rollout; read roadmap record, organizational messages main page and FAQ. No account of existing-message behaviour on arrival was found.

claims.quote: Schedule: Configure the start date, end date, and frequency when the message is sent to users. ... Finish: Review the message before scheduling or sending for approval by your organization's approvers.

claims.claim: Messages can contain text authored by the organization.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Custom messages require approval by someone other than their creator before delivery.
claims.quote: approvers must approve custom messages before the system delivers them to users. Approvers can't approve or reject a message that they created.

claims.claim: Pre-made messages require no approval.
claims.quote: Selecting a pre-made message doesn't require any approval before the message can be delivered to end users.

claims.quote: verify that no device restriction policies block any of the following settings: ... Windows Tips.

claims.claim: Windows message delivery uses a pull model.
claims.quote: Windows delivers messages on a pull model, so the system buffers messages on a set period for each of the channels.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Messages might take 24 or more hours to arrive, so the test should allow at least that long.
claims.quote: Since devices might be configured to request content at different times, messages might take 24 or more hours before the message is received and rendered.

claims.quote: Searched: organizational messages hybrid joined licensing price requirements unmanaged devices; read organizational messages main page and FAQ, and Windows licensing search excerpt. Requirements concern channels and advanced features, not a hybrid-specific entitlement.

claims.fix: Include the omitted headings in controls[0].ui.path: 'Devices > Manage devices > Configuration > Policies > Create > New Policy > Platform > Windows 10 and later > Profile type > Settings catalog > Create > Basics > Configuration settings > Add settings > Settings picker > Browse by category > Experience > Settings name > Enable delivery of organizational messages (User)'. claims.claim: The organizational messages Learn page describes admin time as a cost.

claims.fix: Replace 'The cost it describes is licences for the advanced features and admin time.' with 'The page describes licence requirements for advanced features. Plan for admin time to configure delivery policies and author messages.' This separates documented licensing from the wiki's assessment.
